headline: Ever Given Container Ship Wedged Across Suez Canal Halting Global Maritime Trade
raw_text: The 20,000 TEU ultra-large container ship Ever Given has run aground in the southern single-lane section of Egypt's Suez Canal following high winds and a blinding dust storm, completely blocking maritime traffic in both directions. Over 300 vessels carrying crude oil, automotive components, and consumer electronics are stranded in holding anchorages in the Red Sea and Mediterranean as international salvage teams deploy tugs and dredgers to refloat the 400-meter vessel.

headline: Historic Drought Forces Panama Canal Authority to Slash Daily Ship Transits by Over 30%
raw_text: A severe dry spell exacerbated by the El Niño weather phenomenon has depleted water levels in Gatun Lake, prompting the Panama Canal Authority to restrict daily vessel transits from the standard 36 down to 24 slots, with further reductions planned. Unreserved bulk carriers and container vessels are facing waiting periods of up to three weeks, severely impacting US agricultural grain exports to Asia and Liquefied Petroleum Gas shipments ahead of peak winter demand.

headline: Major Ocean Carriers Reroute Container Fleets Around Cape of Good Hope Following Red Sea Missile Attacks
raw_text: Top container lines including Maersk, MSC, and Hapag-Lloyd have announced indefinite diversions away from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and Suez Canal after commercial vessels came under anti-ship missile and drone attack off the Yemeni coastline. Diverting cargo around the Cape of Good Hope adds 10 to 14 days to Asia-Europe voyages, driving spot container freight rates up by more than 150% and triggering logistical bottlenecks for fast-fashion apparel and automotive manufacturing plants.

headline: Port of Los Angeles and Long Beach Face Historic Backlog as Over 70 Container Ships Idle Offshore
raw_text: An unprecedented flotilla of 73 container ships sits at anchor in San Pedro Bay awaiting berths at the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach. The severe gridlock, triggered by a post-pandemic surge in US consumer electronics and home furniture purchases, is exacerbated by an acute inland shortage of truck chassis, rail freight capacity, and warehouse space, raising fears of empty retail shelves ahead of the holiday shopping season.

headline: Super Typhoon Megumi Forces 72-Hour Operational Shutdown at Port of Shanghai and Ningbo Terminals
raw_text: Category 4 Super Typhoon Megumi has made landfall along the eastern seaboard of China, compelling maritime safety authorities to halt all crane and container handling operations across the Port of Shanghai and nearby Ningbo-Zhoushan. Container vessels have been ordered out to open sea anchorages. Analysts estimate that the three-day shutdown will delay more than 380,000 TEUs of exported clean tech solar panels, lithium batteries, and consumer electronics bound for European and North American markets.

headline: Dockworkers Union Launches 5-Day Strike Across Rotterdam and Antwerp Over Automation Concerns
raw_text: More than 8,000 dockers and gantry crane operators have walked off the job at the ports of Rotterdam and Antwerp-Bruges after negotiations stalled over automated container handling technology and cost-of-living salary increases. The strike has halted gate activity and barge transshipments, cutting off petrochemical deliveries and bulk metal supplies destined for major industrial manufacturers in Germany and the wider Benelux region.

headline: Naval Escorts Deployed to Strait of Hormuz Following Tanker Seizures and Mine Attacks
raw_text: Geopolitical tensions in the Persian Gulf reached a flashpoint after naval commandos seized the British-flagged oil tanker Stena Impero while navigating the Strait of Hormuz. The seizure, occurring alongside a spate of limpet mine explosions on merchant tankers in adjacent waters, has prompted international coalitions to initiate armed maritime escorts, causing crude tanker war-risk insurance premiums to spike tenfold.

headline: Crude Carrier and Barge Collision Shuts Westbound Channel in Strait of Malacca
raw_text: A pre-dawn collision between a laden Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) and a container feeder barge near the narrow Phillips Channel in the Strait of Malacca has resulted in a localized fuel oil spill and navigational hazard. Port and maritime authorities in Singapore and Malaysia have temporarily closed the westbound transit lane to carry out oil containment and salvage operations, forcing hundreds of inbound container ships and tankers into holding positions.

headline: Bulk Carrier Loses Steering and Grounds in Bosphorus Strait Halting Black Sea Grain Transits
raw_text: A 225-meter Panamax bulk carrier laden with 65,000 metric tons of wheat suffered catastrophic rudder failure and ran aground along the Bosphorus Strait near Istanbul. Turkish coastal safety authorities suspended all maritime vessel traffic through the waterway while salvage tugboats were deployed. Over 60 bulk carriers and tankers transporting grain, sunflower oil, and refined fuels from Black Sea ports have been immobilized on either side of the strait.

headline: Real Madrid Clinches Dramatic 3-2 Champions League Victory with Stoppage-Time Header
raw_text: Real Madrid mounted another historic European comeback at the Santiago Bernabéu to defeat Bayern Munich 3-2 on aggregate and advance to the Champions League final. Substitute striker Joselu scored two dramatic goals in the 88th and 91st minutes after Alphonso Davies had put the German giants ahead, sparking jubilant celebrations across the Spanish capital as fans flooded the streets to celebrate the club's bid for a fifteenth European crown.

headline: Pop Star Maya Lin Announces Surprise Engagement and Upcoming World Acoustic Tour
raw_text: Grammy-winning pop sensation Maya Lin surprised millions of fans on Valentine's Day by announcing her engagement to film director Julian Vance via an Instagram post featuring a vintage emerald ring. The singer also revealed dates for an intimate 30-city global acoustic theater tour beginning this autumn in London, with pre-sale tickets set to go live next Tuesday across ticketing platforms.

headline: Severe Flash Flooding Shuts Down Port of Santos Operations for Third Consecutive Day
raw_text: Unprecedented flash flooding driven by record rainfall across the state of São Paulo has inundated the access roads and terminal yards of the Port of Santos — Latin America's busiest cargo port — forcing a complete suspension of container and bulk terminal operations for a third consecutive day. Over 80 vessels, including soybean bulk carriers, refrigerated fruit reefers, and ethanol tankers, are idling at anchor in the Santos Channel awaiting resumption of berth assignments. Terminal operators warn that clearance of waterlogged container yards may require an additional 72 to 96 hours, with knock-on delays expected at inland rail distribution hubs in Campinas and São Paulo.
